sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to with their rank and status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case leading to this appeal are that the petitioners filed petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1998 seeking compensation of Rs.1,25,00,000/- for death of Vinuth in the accident.

It is stated in the claim petition that on 08th July, 2014, Vinuth K M, was proceeding in VRL Volvo bus bearing registration No.KA- 25/D-1400 towards Mumbai from Shivamogga on Bangalore- Pune National Highway and while so performing the journey, on the next day, i.e. on 09th July, 2014 at 5.00 pm, when the bus was moving in the vicinity of Vele village,
near Khabatki tunnel, the driver of the bus lost control and drove the same in rash NC:
2024:KHC-D:8313-DB and negligent manner and dashed to the hill and as a result the said Vinuth sustained grievous injuries and succumbed at the spot.

It is further stated in the claim petition that as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged 24 years, was hale and healthy and has completed Hospitality Management course from SVGH Vocational Training College and completed a program of training and assessment in Food Safety and Catering and also completed training course in Personal Safety and Social Responsibilities, Fire Prevention and Fire Fighting Personnel Survival Techniques, Elementary First Aid form Sea Scan Maritime Foundation and also completed training course in Passenger-ship Familiarisation Course and Crisis Management Operational Level and also completed HACCP Course programme in Mumbai.

The deceased was working as Assistant Waiter in Cruise i.e. MSC Crociere SA through Imperial Ocean Management Private Limited, Mumbai and earning a salary of more than US$ 1,500.00 per month from 15th June 2013 to 04th April, 2014 on contract basis.

It is also contended that during the service he even completed a programme of Smt. Shaila W/O Manjappa K.D vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174117064/

Respondent No.2 filed objections.
Respondent No.1 has not filed objection.
5. The sum and substance of the statement of objections of respondent No.2 is that the petition is false, frivolous and fabricated not tenable in the eye of law.
Further, it is also denied as to the averments made in the claim petition.
It is also contended that the deceased Vinuth K M did not travel in the bus on the date of the alleged accident.
It is admitted that the respondent No.1 is the owner of the bus and the said bus was insured with the respondent No.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The respondent no.2 has no knowledge about the relationship between the deceased and the petitioners and the compensation claimed is very exorbitant.

It is also contended that the legality, validity and authenticity of the alleged qualification and certified are not from notified and recognised educational institutions and the deceased had no income as on the date of the accident.

Further, the driver who was driving the vehicle at the alleged NC:
2024:KHC-D:8313-DB time of accident did not possess, legal, valid and effective driving licence and the owner, knowingly, violated the conditions of the insurance policy.
On all these grounds sought to dismiss the claim petition.
Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues.
6. To prove the case of the petitioners, four witnesses were examined as PWs1 to 4 and forty documents were produced as Exhibits P1 to P40.
Respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf, but marked six documents as R1 to R6 with consent.

Having heard on both sides, the Tribunal has allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.12,70,000/- with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the appellant/claimants have preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

10. Having heard on both sides and perusal of appeal papers and original record, the following point would arise for our consideration:
1.

Whether the appellants have made out a ground to allow the application under Order XLI Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure to remand the matter to the Tribunal to consider the additional evidence sought to be produced by the appellants/claimants;

11. Our answer to the above points is as under:
Point No.1: in the affirmative; Point No.2: as per final order.

Regarding Point No.1:
12.
We have examined the material placed before this Court.
The appellant/claimants have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.1,25,00,000/- for the death of Vinuth KM in the road traffic accident.
The Tribunal allowed the claim petition by holding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver and awarded compensation of Rs.12,70,000/-.
In the petition at Column No.5, the name and address of the employer of the deceased is shown as MSC Crociere SA, in column 6 the monthly income is shown as Rs.1,00,000/- approximate US$1500.00

PW2-Sachin M. Khedekar, Senior Operation Manager, Imperial Ocean Management Private Limited, Mumbai, has deposed that the deceased Vinuth KM worked as Assistant Waiter in Cruise MSC Crociere SA through Imperial Ocean Management Pvt. Ltd. Mumbai and was earning more than US$ 670 per month as salary from 15th June, 2013 to 04th April, 2014 on contract basis.

17. Learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurer has filed statement of objections contending that the application filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of Code of Civil Procedure seeking issuance of witness summons is neither maintainable in law nor on facts.
It is stated that the petitioners have not stated valid reasons in the application, so as to satisfy the requirements of Order XLI Rule 27 of Code of Civil Procedure.
The provision under Order XLI Rule 27 of Code of Civil Procedure relate to production of evidence and not seeking issuance of witness summons.
The appellants have not produced income-tax returns, admittedly the deceased is an Indian citizen.
The date of accident is 09th July, 2015 and as on that date, the deceased - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB was not employed.
Hence, it is contended that there is no merit in the application and sought for dismissal of application.
18. In view of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the function of the Tribunal or Court is to award "just compensation".
The Motor Vehicle Act is beneficial and welfare legislation.
A "just compensation" is one which is reasonable on the basis of the evidence produced on record.
It cannot be said to have become time-barred.
There is no need for new cause of action to claim an enhanced amount.

The courts are duty- bound to award just compensation as observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAMLA v. NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMTED reported in Smt. Shaila W/O Manjappa K.D vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174117064/
6 2019 ACJ 559.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also pertinent here to refer to the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAJWATI (supra), wherein at paragraph 19 of the judgment, it observed as under:
"19.

It is well settled that Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a beneficial piece of legislation and as such,
while dealing with compensation cases, once the actual occurrence of the accident has been established, the Tribunal's role would be to award just and fair compensation.

As held by this Court in Sunita (Supra) and Kusum Lata (Supra), strict rules of evidence as applicable in a criminal trial,
are not applicable in motor accident compensation cases, i.e., to say, "the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases"."

19. Considering the facts and circumstances and also the opinion expressed by the Tribunal, it is just and proper to permit the appellants to produce additional evidence which are required to do substantial justice between the parties.
It is to be noted that due to inadvertence, the claimants might have not produced the proposed additional evidence before the Tribunal.

Since the Tribunal has expressed its opinion that the petitioners have failed to produce the acceptable evidence as to the income of the deceased, the proposed additional evidence is very much required to adjudicate the matter in dispute.
If the application is not allowed, the petitioners would be deprived of getting just and reasonable compensation as to the death of Vinuth who died in the road traffic accident.
It is also the duty of the Court/Tribunal to award just compensation in accordance with law.

Keeping in mind the aforesaid decisions and provisions of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and also the application filed in IA.I of 2024, so also, considering the arguments advanced on behalf of the appellants, it is just and proper to allow the application filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
Hence, we answer point No.1 in the affirmative.
